title: Merit of reciting Bismillah along with La Haula Wa La Quwwata
data:
Seventh: through valid chains of authority, Sayyid Ibn Tawus reported Imam al-Rida (a) as saying: he who repeats the following doxology (zikr) one hundred times after the dawn (fajr) Prayer will be closer to the Greatest Name of Almighty Allah than the blackness of the eye is to its whiteness:
بِسْمِ اللهِ الرَّحْمٰنِ الرَّحِيْمِ لَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ اِلَّا بِاللّٰهِ الْعَلِىِّ الْعَظِيْمِ
BISMILLAAHIR RAHMAANIR RAHEEM, LAA HAWLA WA LAA QUWWATA ILLAA BILLAAHIL A'LIYYIL A'ZEEM
In the Name of Allah, the All-beneficent, the All-merciful: there is no power and no strength except with Allah, the Most High, the All-magnificent.
Through valid chains of authority too, Imam al-Sadiq and Imam al-Kazim (a) are reported to have said, "He who says this doxology (zikr) seven times after the dawn (fajr) Prayer and the Sunset Prayer, before he speaks or moves from his position, Almighty Allah will fend off from him seven kinds of misfortune, the easiest of which are leprosy, mycobacterium, trickeries of Satan, and evils of ruling authorities.
According to other validly reported traditions, this doxology (zikr) may be repeated three or ten times. However, it may be repeated three times as a minimum and one hundred times as a maximum; the more, the better in reward.
